text: External fire near the equipment — External fire heats C-103, causing NMP to vaporize rapidly, pressure to rise, and level to drop as liquid flashes or is lost to relief
Loss of cooling water — Loss of cooling water causes bottoms temperature to rise in C-103 (NMP solvent stripper), changing composition and risking runaway reaction
External fire near the equipment — External fire near C-103 (NMP solvent stripper) changes composition by heating and possible decomposition

Heat exchanger tube ruptures — Tube rupture could allow high‑pressure vapor to enter the cooling‑water side, raising pressure in the exchanger and potentially causing over‑pressure leakage or rupture.

Heat exchanger tube ruptures — Tube rupture could allow process fluid to leak into the cooling medium side (or vice versa), causing pressure/temperature excursions, flow disruption, mixing of streams, and potential reverse flow depending on pressures.
Loss of cooling water — NMP liquid in C-103 boils away or drains to the bottom, causing dry-out and possible overheat of the reboiler/stripping section
Safety interlock or trip operates spuriously — NMP level in C-103 drops below normal operating level; if feed continues, the column may run dry and the reboiler may overheat
Safety interlock or trip operates spuriously — Safety interlock or trip operates spuriously, potentially isolating C-103 or driving an unwanted composition change
Control loop sensor or controller gives a wrong signal — Process composition changes in C-103 as control of bottoms temperature and flow is lost
Heat exchanger tube ruptures — Loss of cooling water through a ruptured tube reduces heat removal, allowing the condensing vapor temperature to rise above design limits.
